components.text: Warm-up: Sharing a Pizza Fairly

Imagine a pizza cut into 8 equal slices shared among 4 friends. How many slices does each friend get? Talk with a partner about why the slices must be the same size. This is the heart of fractions: we split a whole into equal parts and count how many we have.

components.body: Equal parts mean every piece is the same size and shape. If pieces are different sizes, we cannot write a fair fraction.

components.text: Quick recall: share one example of something you have divided equally at home or school — sharing candy, cutting a sandwich, splitting play time.
Defining a Fraction

A fraction is a way to name part of a whole. It is written as one number on top of another, like 3/4. The bottom number is the denominator: it tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. The top number is the numerator: it tells how many of those equal parts we are talking about.

components.text: Which fraction is larger: 3/8 or 5/8?

components.text: Adding Fractions with Like Denominators

components.text: Read each question carefully and choose the best answer.
In the fraction 3/7, which number is the denominator?
components.explain: The denominator is the bottom number in a fraction. It tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. In 3/7, the denominator is 7.

wrong_reasons.A: 3 is the numerator (the top number), which tells how many parts are being considered.
wrong_reasons.C: 10 is the sum of the numerator and denominator, not the denominator itself.
wrong_reasons.D: 4 is the difference between the denominator and numerator, not the denominator.

components.essence: Identifying the denominator as the bottom number of a fraction
components.tip: De-nominator = 'names' the parts and sits at the Down-bottom.

components.text: A circle is divided into 8 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction represents the shaded portion?
components.explain: The numerator (top number) counts the shaded parts (5), and the denominator (bottom number) counts the total equal parts (8). So the fraction is 5/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 8/5 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts should be on the bottom.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/8 would represent the unshaded parts, not the shaded parts.
wrong_reasons.D: 5/3 reverses the relationship and does not match the model.

components.essence: Writing a fraction from a visual model: shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Shaded on top, total on bottom — 'some over all'.

components.text: In the fraction 3/5, what does the number 3 represent?

options.B: The total number of equal parts

components.explain: The numerator is the top number and tells how many parts are selected or counted. In 3/5, the numerator 3 means 3 parts are being considered out of 5.

wrong_reasons.A: The denominator is the bottom number, not the top.
wrong_reasons.B: The total number of equal parts is the denominator (5), not the numerator.
wrong_reasons.D: A fraction's top number is not a decimal value.

components.essence: Numerator counts the parts selected; denominator names the total parts
components.tip: Numera-tor = the Number you Nu-count on top.

components.text: Which fraction is a proper fraction?
components.explain: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. In 3/4, the numerator (3) is less than the denominator (4), so it is a proper fraction.

wrong_reasons.A: 7/4 is an improper fraction because the numerator (7) is greater than the denominator (4).
wrong_reasons.B: 5/5 equals exactly 1 whole — the numerator equals the denominator, so it is not a proper fraction.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because the numerator (9) is greater than the denominator (2).

components.essence: Proper fractions have numerator < denominator
components.tip: Proper = 'smaller on top' — the part is less than the whole.

components.text: Which symbol correctly compares 3/8 and 5/8?
components.explain: When two fractions have the same denominator, the fraction with the larger numerator is greater. Since 5 > 3, we have 5/8 > 3/8, which means 3/8 < 5/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 3/8 is smaller than 5/8 because 3 < 5 when the denominators are equal.
wrong_reasons.C: The fractions are not equal because the numerators are different (3 ≠ 5).
wrong_reasons.D: Fractions with the same denominator can always be compared by looking at the numerators.

components.essence: Comparing fractions with like denominators: larger numerator means larger fraction
components.tip: Same bottom? Just compare the tops — bigger top means bigger fraction.

components.text: What is 2/6 + 3/6?
components.explain: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same: 2 + 3 = 5, so 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6.

wrong_reasons.A: 5/12 incorrectly adds the denominators — the denominator stays the same when adding like fractions.
wrong_reasons.C: 1/6 would be the result of subtracting 3/6 − 2/6, not adding.
wrong_reasons.D: 6/5 reverses the fraction and incorrectly changes both numbers.

components.essence: Adding fractions with like denominators: add numerators, keep denominator
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: The total parts are 9 and 2 are shaded, so 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/7 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts must be the denominator.
wrong_reasons.D: 11/9 adds the shaded and total parts instead of subtracting, and exceeds 1 whole.

components.essence: Finding the complement fraction: total parts minus shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Unshaded = total minus shaded, all over the total.

components.text: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/5?
components.explain: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: 2 × 2 = 4, 5 × 2 = 10, giving 4/10. Two fractions are equivalent when multiplying or dividing both parts by the same non-zero number gives the same fraction.

wrong_reasons.B: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, not equivalent to 2/5.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/5 is a different fraction, not equivalent.
wrong_reasons.D: 2/6 simplifies to 1/3, not equivalent.

components.essence: Finding equivalent fractions by scaling numerator and denominator equally
components.tip: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the SAME number to find equivalents.

sections.title: Answer Key
sections.content:
Question 1: B (Denominator of 3/7 is 7).
Question 2: B (5 shaded out of 8 total parts = 5/8).
Question 3: C (The numerator 3 represents the parts being counted).
Question 4: C (3/4 is proper because 3 < 4).
Question 5: B (3/8 < 5/8 because 3 < 5 with the same denominator).
Question 6: B (2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6; add numerators, keep denominator).
Question 7: B (9 − 2 = 7 unshaded parts, so 7/9 is unshaded).
Question 8: A (2/5 × 2/2 = 4/10).

Scoring guide: 7–8 correct = Mastery; 5–6 correct = Proficient; 3–4 correct = Developing; 0–2 correct = Needs reteaching of fraction basics.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/7 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts must be the denominator.
wrong_reasons.D: 11/9 adds the shaded and total parts instead of subtracting, and exceeds 1 whole.

components.essence: Finding the complement fraction: total parts minus shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Unshaded = total minus shaded, all over the total.

components.text: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/5?

wrong_reasons.B: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, not equivalent to 2/5.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/5 is a different fraction, not equivalent.

wrong_reasons.A: 7/4 is an improper fraction because the numerator (7) is greater than the denominator (4).
wrong_reasons.B: 5/5 equals exactly 1 whole — the numerator equals the denominator, so it is not a proper fraction.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because the numerator (9) is greater than the denominator (2).

components.essence: Proper fractions have numerator < denominator
components.tip: Proper = 'smaller on top' — the part is less than the whole.

components.text: Which symbol correctly compares 3/8 and 5/8?
components.explain: When two fractions have the same denominator, the fraction with the larger numerator is greater. Since 5 > 3, we have 5/8 > 3/8, which means 3/8 < 5/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 3/8 is smaller than 5/8 because 3 < 5 when the denominators are equal.
wrong_reasons.C: The fractions are not equal because the numerators are different (3 ≠ 5).
wrong_reasons.D: Fractions with the same denominator can always be compared by looking at the numerators.

components.essence: Comparing fractions with like denominators: larger numerator means larger fraction
components.tip: Same bottom? Just compare the tops — bigger top means bigger fraction.

components.text: What is 2/6 + 3/6?
components.explain: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same: 2 + 3 = 5, so 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6.

wrong_reasons.A: 5/12 incorrectly adds the denominators — the denominator stays the same when adding like fractions.
wrong_reasons.C: 1/6 would be the result of subtracting 3/6 − 2/6, not adding.
wrong_reasons.D: 6/5 reverses the fraction and incorrectly changes both numbers.

components.essence: Adding fractions with like denominators: add numerators, keep denominator
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: The total parts are 9 and 2 are shaded, so 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/7 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts must be the denominator.
wrong_reasons.D: 11/9 adds the shaded and total parts instead of subtracting, and exceeds 1 whole.

components.essence: Finding the complement fraction: total parts minus shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Unshaded = total minus shaded, all over the total.

components.text: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/5?
components.explain: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: 2 × 2 = 4, 5 × 2 = 10, giving 4/10. Two fractions are equivalent when multiplying or dividing both parts by the same non-zero number gives the same fraction.

wrong_reasons.B: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, not equivalent to 2/5.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/5 is a different fraction, not equivalent.
wrong_reasons.D: 2/6 simplifies to 1/3, not equivalent.

components.essence: Finding equivalent fractions by scaling numerator and denominator equally
components.tip: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the SAME number to find equivalents.

components.text: Multiple Choice Questions
Read each question carefully. Choose the best answer. Each question is worth 1 point for a total of 8 points.
In the fraction 3/4, what does the number 4 represent?

options.A: The number of parts we have
options.B: The total number of equal parts the whole is divided into
options.C: The number of parts that are not shaded

components.explain: The denominator (bottom number) tells us the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into. In 3/4, the 4 means the whole is split into 4 equal parts.

wrong_reasons.A: The number of parts we have is the numerator (top number), which is 3, not 4.
wrong_reasons.C: The number of unshaded parts would be 1 (4 − 3 = 1), not 4.
wrong_reasons.D: The whole is represented by 1 (or 4/4), not by the denominator alone.

components.essence: Denominator = total equal parts of the whole
components.tip: De-nominator = how many parts make the whole. Think 'D' for 'divided into'.

components.text: Which fraction represents a circle divided into 6 equal parts with 5 parts shaded?
components.explain: The numerator (top) counts the shaded parts (5), and the denominator (bottom) counts the total equal parts (6). So the fraction is 5/6.

wrong_reasons.A: 6/5 reverses the numbers — the shaded parts go on top, total parts on the bottom.
wrong_reasons.B: 1/6 would mean only 1 part is shaded, not 5.
wrong_reasons.D: 5/1 would mean 5 wholes, not 5 out of 6 parts.

components.essence: Numerator = shaded parts; Denominator = total parts
components.tip: Shaded over Total = Fraction. Top = what you see, Bottom = what there is.

components.text: Which fraction is larger: 3/8 or 5/8?
components.explain: When denominators are the same, the fraction with the larger numerator is larger. Since 5 > 3, 5/8 is larger than 3/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 3/8 has fewer parts out of the same 8, so it is smaller, not larger.
wrong_reasons.C: They are not equal because 5 ≠ 3 — the numerators are different.
wrong_reasons.D: They CAN be compared because the denominators are the same (both 8).

components.essence: Same denominator → compare numerators directly
components.tip: Same bottom? Just compare the tops. Bigger top = bigger fraction.

components.text: What is 2/7 + 3/7?
components.explain: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator: 2 + 3 = 5, so 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.

wrong_reasons.A: 5/14 would mean you added both numerators AND denominators — denominators stay the same.
wrong_reasons.C: 6/7 would be the result if you multiplied 2 × 3 = 6 instead of adding 2 + 3 = 5.
wrong_reasons.D: 1/7 would be the result of subtraction (3 − 2 = 1), not addition.

components.essence: Add numerators only; denominator stays the same
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom. Never add denominators.

components.text: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. You eat 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did you eat?
components.explain: You ate 3 slices out of 8 total slices. The fraction is 3/8 (eaten parts over total parts).

wrong_reasons.A: 8/3 reverses the fraction — total slices go on the bottom, eaten slices on top.
wrong_reasons.C: 5/8 is the fraction REMAINING (8 − 3 = 5), not the fraction eaten.
wrong_reasons.D: 3/5 uses the wrong total — there are 8 slices, not 5.

components.essence: Part over Whole = Fraction
components.tip: What you ate (3) over what there was (8) = 3/8.

components.text: Which of the following is a proper fraction?
components.explain: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. In 3/4, 3 < 4, so it is a proper fraction.

wrong_reasons.A: 7/4 is an improper fraction because 7 > 4 (numerator is larger than denominator).
wrong_reasons.B: 5/5 equals 1 whole — the numerator equals the denominator, so it is not a proper fraction.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because 9 > 2.

components.essence: Proper fraction: numerator < denominator
components.tip: Proper = smaller on top. If the top is bigger or equal, it's not proper.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts. If 2 parts are shaded, what fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: If 2 out of 9 parts are shaded, then 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the fraction that is not shaded.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/2 reverses the fraction and does not represent the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/7 reverses the fraction and uses the wrong numbers.

components.essence: Unshaded = Total parts − Shaded parts
components.tip: Not shaded = Total (9) minus Shaded (2) = 7. So 7/9.

components.text: Which statement about the fraction 4/6 is correct?

options.A: The numerator is 6 and the denominator is 4
options.B: The whole is divided into 4 equal parts and 6 are selected
options.C: The whole is divided into 6 equal parts and 4 are selected

components.explain: In 4/6, the denominator (6) means the whole is divided into 6 equal parts, and the numerator (4) means 4 of those parts are selected or shaded.

wrong_reasons.A: The numerator is 4 (top) and the denominator is 6 (bottom) — these are reversed.
wrong_reasons.B: This swaps the numbers — 6 is the denominator (total parts), not the numerator.
wrong_reasons.D: 4/6 is less than 1 because the numerator (4) is smaller than the denominator (6).

components.essence: Numerator = selected parts; Denominator = total equal parts
components.tip: Top = how many you have. Bottom = how many make a whole.

wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because the numerator (9) is greater than the denominator (2).

wrong_reasons.A: 5/12 incorrectly adds the denominators — the denominator stays the same when adding like fractions.
wrong_reasons.C: 1/6 would be the result of subtracting 3/6 − 2/6, not adding.
wrong_reasons.D: 6/5 reverses the fraction and incorrectly changes both numbers.

components.essence: Adding fractions with like denominators: add numerators, keep denominator
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: The total parts are 9 and 2 are shaded, so 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/7 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts must be the denominator.
wrong_reasons.D: 11/9 adds the shaded and total parts instead of subtracting, and exceeds 1 whole.

components.essence: Finding the complement fraction: total parts minus shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Unshaded = total minus shaded, all over the total.

components.text: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/5?

wrong_reasons.B: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, not equivalent to 2/5.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/5 is a different fraction, not equivalent.
wrong_reasons.D: 2/6 simplifies to 1/3, not equivalent.

components.essence: Finding equivalent fractions by scaling numerator and denominator equally
components.tip: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the SAME number to find equivalents.

components.text: Read each question carefully and choose the best answer.
In the fraction 3/7, which number is the denominator?
components.explain: The denominator is the bottom number in a fraction. It tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. In 3/7, the denominator is 7.

wrong_reasons.A: 3 is the numerator (the top number), which tells how many parts are being considered.
wrong_reasons.C: 10 is the sum of the numerator and denominator, not the denominator itself.
wrong_reasons.D: 4 is the difference between the denominator and numerator, not the denominator.

components.essence: Identifying the denominator as the bottom number of a fraction
components.tip: De-nominator = 'names' the parts and sits at the Down-bottom.

components.text: A circle is divided into 8 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction represents the shaded portion?
components.explain: The numerator (top number) counts the shaded parts (5), and the denominator (bottom number) counts the total equal parts (8). So the fraction is 5/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 8/5 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts should be on the bottom.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/8 would represent the unshaded parts, not the shaded parts.
wrong_reasons.D: 5/3 reverses the relationship and does not match the model.

components.essence: Writing a fraction from a visual model: shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Shaded on top, total on bottom — 'some over all'.

components.text: In the fraction 3/5, what does the number 3 represent?

options.B: The total number of equal parts

components.explain: The numerator is the top number and tells how many parts are selected or counted. In 3/5, the numerator 3 means 3 parts are being considered out of 5.

wrong_reasons.A: The denominator is the bottom number, not the top.
wrong_reasons.B: The total number of equal parts is the denominator (5), not the numerator.
wrong_reasons.D: A fraction's top number is not a decimal value.

components.essence: Numerator counts the parts selected; denominator names the total parts
components.tip: Numera-tor = the Number you Nu-count on top.

components.text: Which fraction is a proper fraction?
components.explain: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. In 3/4, the numerator (3) is less than the denominator (4), so it is a proper fraction.

wrong_reasons.A: 7/4 is an improper fraction because the numerator (7) is greater than the denominator (4).
wrong_reasons.B: 5/5 equals exactly 1 whole — the numerator equals the denominator, so it is not a proper fraction.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because the numerator (9) is greater than the denominator (2).

components.essence: Proper fractions have numerator < denominator
components.tip: Proper = 'smaller on top' — the part is less than the whole.

components.text: Which symbol correctly compares 3/8 and 5/8?
components.explain: When two fractions have the same denominator, the fraction with the larger numerator is greater. Since 5 > 3, we have 5/8 > 3/8, which means 3/8 < 5/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 3/8 is smaller than 5/8 because 3 < 5 when the denominators are equal.
wrong_reasons.C: The fractions are not equal because the numerators are different (3 ≠ 5).
wrong_reasons.D: Fractions with the same denominator can always be compared by looking at the numerators.

components.essence: Comparing fractions with like denominators: larger numerator means larger fraction
components.tip: Same bottom? Just compare the tops — bigger top means bigger fraction.

components.text: What is 2/6 + 3/6?
components.explain: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same: 2 + 3 = 5, so 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6.

wrong_reasons.A: 5/12 incorrectly adds the denominators — the denominator stays the same when adding like fractions.
wrong_reasons.C: 1/6 would be the result of subtracting 3/6 − 2/6, not adding.
wrong_reasons.D: 6/5 reverses the fraction and incorrectly changes both numbers.

components.essence: Adding fractions with like denominators: add numerators, keep denominator
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: The total parts are 9 and 2 are shaded, so 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/7 reverses the numerator and denominator — the total parts must be the denominator.
wrong_reasons.D: 11/9 adds the shaded and total parts instead of subtracting, and exceeds 1 whole.

components.essence: Finding the complement fraction: total parts minus shaded parts over total parts
components.tip: Unshaded = total minus shaded, all over the total.

components.text: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/5?
components.explain: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: 2 × 2 = 4, 5 × 2 = 10, giving 4/10. Two fractions are equivalent when multiplying or dividing both parts by the same non-zero number gives the same fraction.

wrong_reasons.B: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, not equivalent to 2/5.
wrong_reasons.C: 3/5 is a different fraction, not equivalent.
wrong_reasons.D: 2/6 simplifies to 1/3, not equivalent.

components.essence: Finding equivalent fractions by scaling numerator and denominator equally
components.tip: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the SAME number to find equivalents.

Question 2: B (5 shaded out of 8 total parts = 5/8).
Question 3: C (The numerator 3 represents the parts being counted).
Question 4: C (3/4 is proper because 3 < 4).
Question 5: B (3/8 < 5/8 because 3 < 5 with the same denominator).

components.text: Warm-up: Sharing a Pizza Fairly

Imagine a pizza cut into 8 equal slices shared among 4 friends. How many slices does each friend get? Talk with a partner about why the slices must be the same size. This is the heart of fractions: we split a whole into equal parts and count how many we have.

components.body: Equal parts mean every piece is the same size and shape. If pieces are different sizes, we cannot write a fair fraction.

components.text: Quick recall: share one example of something you have divided equally at home or school — sharing candy, cutting a sandwich, splitting play time.
Defining a Fraction

A fraction is a way to name part of a whole. It is written as one number on top of another, like 3/4. The bottom number is the denominator: it tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. The top number is the numerator: it tells how many of those equal parts we are talking about.

components.text: Multiple Choice Questions
Read each question carefully. Choose the best answer. Each question is worth 1 point for a total of 8 points.
In the fraction 3/4, what does the number 4 represent?

options.A: The number of parts we have
options.B: The total number of equal parts the whole is divided into
options.C: The number of parts that are not shaded

components.explain: The denominator (bottom number) tells us the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into. In 3/4, the 4 means the whole is split into 4 equal parts.

wrong_reasons.A: The number of parts we have is the numerator (top number), which is 3, not 4.
wrong_reasons.C: The number of unshaded parts would be 1 (4 − 3 = 1), not 4.
wrong_reasons.D: The whole is represented by 1 (or 4/4), not by the denominator alone.

components.essence: Denominator = total equal parts of the whole
components.tip: De-nominator = how many parts make the whole. Think 'D' for 'divided into'.

components.text: Which fraction represents a circle divided into 6 equal parts with 5 parts shaded?
components.explain: The numerator (top) counts the shaded parts (5), and the denominator (bottom) counts the total equal parts (6). So the fraction is 5/6.

wrong_reasons.A: 6/5 reverses the numbers — the shaded parts go on top, total parts on the bottom.
wrong_reasons.B: 1/6 would mean only 1 part is shaded, not 5.
wrong_reasons.D: 5/1 would mean 5 wholes, not 5 out of 6 parts.

components.essence: Numerator = shaded parts; Denominator = total parts
components.tip: Shaded over Total = Fraction. Top = what you see, Bottom = what there is.

components.text: Which fraction is larger: 3/8 or 5/8?
components.explain: When denominators are the same, the fraction with the larger numerator is larger. Since 5 > 3, 5/8 is larger than 3/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 3/8 has fewer parts out of the same 8, so it is smaller, not larger.
wrong_reasons.C: They are not equal because 5 ≠ 3 — the numerators are different.
wrong_reasons.D: They CAN be compared because the denominators are the same (both 8).

components.essence: Same denominator → compare numerators directly
components.tip: Same bottom? Just compare the tops. Bigger top = bigger fraction.

components.text: What is 2/7 + 3/7?
components.explain: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator: 2 + 3 = 5, so 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.

wrong_reasons.A: 5/14 would mean you added both numerators AND denominators — denominators stay the same.
wrong_reasons.C: 6/7 would be the result if you multiplied 2 × 3 = 6 instead of adding 2 + 3 = 5.
wrong_reasons.D: 1/7 would be the result of subtraction (3 − 2 = 1), not addition.

components.essence: Add numerators only; denominator stays the same
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom. Never add denominators.

components.text: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. You eat 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did you eat?
components.explain: You ate 3 slices out of 8 total slices. The fraction is 3/8 (eaten parts over total parts).

wrong_reasons.A: 8/3 reverses the fraction — total slices go on the bottom, eaten slices on top.
wrong_reasons.C: 5/8 is the fraction REMAINING (8 − 3 = 5), not the fraction eaten.
wrong_reasons.D: 3/5 uses the wrong total — there are 8 slices, not 5.

components.essence: Part over Whole = Fraction
components.tip: What you ate (3) over what there was (8) = 3/8.

components.text: Which of the following is a proper fraction?
components.explain: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. In 3/4, 3 < 4, so it is a proper fraction.

wrong_reasons.A: 7/4 is an improper fraction because 7 > 4 (numerator is larger than denominator).
wrong_reasons.B: 5/5 equals 1 whole — the numerator equals the denominator, so it is not a proper fraction.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because 9 > 2.

components.essence: Proper fraction: numerator < denominator
components.tip: Proper = smaller on top. If the top is bigger or equal, it's not proper.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts. If 2 parts are shaded, what fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: If 2 out of 9 parts are shaded, then 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the fraction that is not shaded.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/2 reverses the fraction and does not represent the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/7 reverses the fraction and uses the wrong numbers.

components.essence: Unshaded = Total parts − Shaded parts
components.tip: Not shaded = Total (9) minus Shaded (2) = 7. So 7/9.

components.text: Which statement about the fraction 4/6 is correct?

options.A: The numerator is 6 and the denominator is 4
options.B: The whole is divided into 4 equal parts and 6 are selected
options.C: The whole is divided into 6 equal parts and 4 are selected

components.explain: In 4/6, the denominator (6) means the whole is divided into 6 equal parts, and the numerator (4) means 4 of those parts are selected or shaded.

wrong_reasons.A: The numerator is 4 (top) and the denominator is 6 (bottom) — these are reversed.
wrong_reasons.B: This swaps the numbers — 6 is the denominator (total parts), not the numerator.
wrong_reasons.D: 4/6 is less than 1 because the numerator (4) is smaller than the denominator (6).

components.essence: Numerator = selected parts; Denominator = total equal parts
components.tip: Top = how many you have. Bottom = how many make a whole.

components.caption: Total: 8 points. Distribute based on class performance. Score 6–8: Exceeds; 4–5: Meets; 0–3: Needs reteaching.

Question 4: B — 1 + 2 = 3 numerator; denominator stays 4 → 3/4.
Question 5: B — 9 is the bottom number, so it is the denominator.
Question 6: B — Three out of six equal parts is written 3/6.
Question 7: B — Same denominator 7; 5 > 2 makes 5/7 larger.
Question 8: B — 1 + 2 = 3 numerator; denominator stays 6 → 3/6.
Question 9: A — 3 pieces eaten out of 8 total pieces is 3/8.

components.text: Multiple Choice Questions
Read each question carefully. Choose the best answer. Each question is worth 1 point for a total of 8 points.
In the fraction 3/4, what does the number 4 represent?

options.A: The number of parts we have
options.B: The total number of equal parts the whole is divided into
options.C: The number of parts that are not shaded

components.explain: The denominator (bottom number) tells us the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into. In 3/4, the 4 means the whole is split into 4 equal parts.

wrong_reasons.A: The number of parts we have is the numerator (top number), which is 3, not 4.
wrong_reasons.C: The number of unshaded parts would be 1 (4 − 3 = 1), not 4.
wrong_reasons.D: The whole is represented by 1 (or 4/4), not by the denominator alone.

components.essence: Denominator = total equal parts of the whole
components.tip: De-nominator = how many parts make the whole. Think 'D' for 'divided into'.

components.text: Which fraction represents a circle divided into 6 equal parts with 5 parts shaded?
components.explain: The numerator (top) counts the shaded parts (5), and the denominator (bottom) counts the total equal parts (6). So the fraction is 5/6.

wrong_reasons.A: 6/5 reverses the numbers — the shaded parts go on top, total parts on the bottom.
wrong_reasons.B: 1/6 would mean only 1 part is shaded, not 5.
wrong_reasons.D: 5/1 would mean 5 wholes, not 5 out of 6 parts.

components.essence: Numerator = shaded parts; Denominator = total parts
components.tip: Shaded over Total = Fraction. Top = what you see, Bottom = what there is.

components.text: Which fraction is larger: 3/8 or 5/8?
components.explain: When denominators are the same, the fraction with the larger numerator is larger. Since 5 > 3, 5/8 is larger than 3/8.

wrong_reasons.A: 3/8 has fewer parts out of the same 8, so it is smaller, not larger.
wrong_reasons.C: They are not equal because 5 ≠ 3 — the numerators are different.
wrong_reasons.D: They CAN be compared because the denominators are the same (both 8).

components.essence: Same denominator → compare numerators directly
components.tip: Same bottom? Just compare the tops. Bigger top = bigger fraction.

components.text: What is 2/7 + 3/7?
components.explain: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator: 2 + 3 = 5, so 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.

wrong_reasons.A: 5/14 would mean you added both numerators AND denominators — denominators stay the same.
wrong_reasons.C: 6/7 would be the result if you multiplied 2 × 3 = 6 instead of adding 2 + 3 = 5.
wrong_reasons.D: 1/7 would be the result of subtraction (3 − 2 = 1), not addition.

components.essence: Add numerators only; denominator stays the same
components.tip: Same bottom? Add the tops, keep the bottom. Never add denominators.

components.text: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. You eat 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did you eat?
components.explain: You ate 3 slices out of 8 total slices. The fraction is 3/8 (eaten parts over total parts).

wrong_reasons.A: 8/3 reverses the fraction — total slices go on the bottom, eaten slices on top.
wrong_reasons.C: 5/8 is the fraction REMAINING (8 − 3 = 5), not the fraction eaten.
wrong_reasons.D: 3/5 uses the wrong total — there are 8 slices, not 5.

components.essence: Part over Whole = Fraction
components.tip: What you ate (3) over what there was (8) = 3/8.

components.text: Which of the following is a proper fraction?
components.explain: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. In 3/4, 3 < 4, so it is a proper fraction.

wrong_reasons.A: 7/4 is an improper fraction because 7 > 4 (numerator is larger than denominator).
wrong_reasons.B: 5/5 equals 1 whole — the numerator equals the denominator, so it is not a proper fraction.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/2 is an improper fraction because 9 > 2.

components.essence: Proper fraction: numerator < denominator
components.tip: Proper = smaller on top. If the top is bigger or equal, it's not proper.

components.text: A rectangle is divided into 9 equal parts. If 2 parts are shaded, what fraction of the rectangle is NOT shaded?
components.explain: If 2 out of 9 parts are shaded, then 9 − 2 = 7 parts are not shaded. The unshaded fraction is 7/9.

wrong_reasons.A: 2/9 is the fraction that IS shaded, not the fraction that is not shaded.
wrong_reasons.C: 9/2 reverses the fraction and does not represent the unshaded portion.
wrong_reasons.D: 9/7 reverses the fraction and uses the wrong numbers.

components.essence: Unshaded = Total parts − Shaded parts
components.tip: Not shaded = Total (9) minus Shaded (2) = 7. So 7/9.

components.text: Which statement about the fraction 4/6 is correct?

options.A: The numerator is 6 and the denominator is 4
options.B: The whole is divided into 4 equal parts and 6 are selected
options.C: The whole is divided into 6 equal parts and 4 are selected

components.explain: In 4/6, the denominator (6) means the whole is divided into 6 equal parts, and the numerator (4) means 4 of those parts are selected or shaded.

wrong_reasons.A: The numerator is 4 (top) and the denominator is 6 (bottom) — these are reversed.
wrong_reasons.B: This swaps the numbers — 6 is the denominator (total parts), not the numerator.
wrong_reasons.D: 4/6 is less than 1 because the numerator (4) is smaller than the denominator (6).

components.essence: Numerator = selected parts; Denominator = total equal parts
components.tip: Top = how many you have. Bottom = how many make a whole.
